summary: Klamath NF ground lookout near Callahan, CA: built as early as 1915, staffed in 1915 and 1921; only a foundation remains per the register; no access source found.

facts.design: Ground cabin with an unusual window arrangement, possibly a California Region 5 Plan 4A design
facts.status_note: Only a foundation remains at the site, per the FFLOS register; removal date unknown
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Klamath National Forest

events.note: Register says it may have been built as early as 1915; a June 1915 record already refers to the lookout
October 1915: a Mr. Corey and his wife were at the lookout
October 1915: fire near Granite Creek reported from the lookout and put out by a U.S. ranger and a state firewarden
October 1921: a Mr. Friday was filling the fire warden position at the lookout station
Registered April 16, 2020 as US 2020, CA 137; nominated by Brad Eells

notes_for_editor: The 1915 to 1921 staffing and the 1915 fire come from newspaper items and a forest chronology that the Forest Lookouts page quotes; the originals were not checked. No source found describes the site today or gives access, so there is no access key and the story says so. Paradise Craggy is a separate lookout and was not used. Brief record matches the register (ground, gone, US 2020, CA 137); no correction needed.
